Reproducing Mantas, Contestabile, Skara et al. (2024) from dandiset 001828¶

Paper. Mantas I, Contestabile A, Skara V, et al. (2024). Anxa1+ dopamine neuron vulnerability defines prodromal Parkinson's disease bradykinesia and procedural motor learning impairment. bioRxiv, doi:10.1101/2024.12.22.629963. The claims file (claims/001828/10.1101-2024.12.22.629963.yaml) was written from the full text of preprint version 1 (Results, Methods, legends of Figures 1 to 6); the supplementary figures were not in the text read.

Dandiset. DANDI:001828, version 0.261020.1002 (doi:10.48324/dandi.001828/0.261020.1002). The paper cites no version of the dandiset (it was created after the preprint). This is the only published version, so it is pinned; the draft holds the same 1014 assets (checked below).

What the dandiset holds. Behaviour and fiber photometry only: open field sessions with DeepLabCut pose, kinematics and VAME motif labels (Figures 4 and 5), optogenetically evoked dLight release (Figure S2), water drop sessions with photometry (Figure 3D to 3G), forelimb reaching with annotated reaches (Figure 6E to 6J) and arrow maze sessions with pose (Figure 6A to 6D). There is no histology, RNA-seq, qPCR or nosepoke data, and the arrow maze has no end-zone entries or rewards.

Outside inputs. GEO GSE282753, the paper's RNA-seq deposit, read for fig1b only: its count table (GSE282753_counts_mitopark.txt.gz, md5 printed in the data check) holds the MitoPark half of what the claim needs, and that half is run.

import time
import warnings

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests

import anxa1

pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 400)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)

started = time.time()
assets = anxa1.list_assets()
nwb = assets[assets.path.str.endswith(".nwb")].copy()
nwb["kind"] = np.select(
    [nwb.path.str.endswith("behavior+image.nwb"),
     nwb.path.str.contains("ses-oft") & ~nwb.path.str.contains("behavior"),
     nwb.path.str.contains("ses-reaching"),
     nwb.path.str.contains("ses-tmaze") & nwb.path.str.endswith("_image.nwb")],
    ["open field", "evoked release", "reaching", "arrow maze"], "other")
print(f"dandiset {anxa1.DANDISET_ID} version {anxa1.DANDISET_VERSION}: {len(assets)} assets, "
      f"{len(nwb)} NWB files, {(~assets.path.str.endswith('.nwb')).sum()} external videos")
print(nwb.kind.value_counts().to_string())

def load(kind, fn):
    sel = nwb[nwb.kind == kind]
    out = anxa1.load_many(fn, list(sel.asset_id))
    for s, p in zip(out, sel.path):
        s["path"] = p
    return out

t0 = time.time(); oft = load("open field", anxa1.load_oft); print(f"open field {len(oft)} files, {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
t0 = time.time(); opto = load("evoked release", anxa1.load_opto); print(f"evoked release {len(opto)} files, {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
t0 = time.time(); reach = load("reaching", anxa1.load_reach); print(f"reaching {len(reach)} files, {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
t0 = time.time(); maze = load("arrow maze", anxa1.load_maze); print(f"arrow maze {len(maze)} files, {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")

The draft holds the same assets as the pinned version. The archive's summary counts 179 subjects, which matches the distinct subject ids in the files. Its variableMeasured lists only ProcessingModule and BehavioralTimeSeries, though the files also hold fiber photometry.

The groups of Figure 5 are all present, with exactly the legend's numbers of mice. 84 of the 160 open field files are named ses-tmaze-..., and these and the two files without a session in their name have session_id tmaze-... (86 in the table), although their descriptions, contents (VAME labels, kinematics, the open field DeepLabCut model) and frame counts are those of open field sessions. Three experiments are not in the preprint (oft_6ohda_tailStriatum, oft_anti_anxa1) and are left out. Sessions without photometry have 9000 pose frames (5 min at 30 fps); kinematics and motif labels have 30 frames fewer, the VAME time window. Six mice were recorded both as MP-early and as MP-middle, at two ages; the paper's groups treat them as separate samples, and so does this notebook.

The stored speeds are cm/s (unit m/s with conversion 0.01), equal to distance_moved times 30 frames per s, with plausible values for a mouse. Their ratio to the pose displacement is close to the 20 pixels per cm that an 800 pixel image of a 40 cm box gives, so the scale is consistent with the data. No two files share a speed trace.

fp = [s for s in oft if s["fp"]]
rows = []
for s in fp:
    z, off = anxa1.z_on_frames(s)
    tz = s["z_t0"] + np.arange(len(z)) / s["z_rate"]
    smooth = np.convolve(s["dff"], np.ones(12) / 12, mode="same")      # 0.2 s running mean at 60 Hz
    match = {lag: np.corrcoef(z, np.interp(tz + lag, s["dff_t"], smooth))[0, 1] for lag in np.round(np.arange(-0.3, 0.31, 0.05), 2)}
    runs = np.diff(np.r_[0, np.flatnonzero(np.diff(z) != 0) + 1, len(z)])
    zz, v, _ = anxa1.frame_aligned(s)
    ok = np.isfinite(zz) & np.isfinite(v)
    lags = np.arange(-90, 91, 3)
    n = ok.sum(); a, b = zz[ok], v[ok]
    cc = [np.corrcoef(a[max(0, -l):n - max(0, l)], b[max(0, l):n - max(0, -l)])[0, 1] for l in lags]
    rows.append({"group": s["group"], "subject": s["subject"], "start": s["start"][:16], "location": s["location"],
                 "indicator": s["indicator"], "z_samples": len(z), "z_minutes": len(z) / 30 / 60,
                 "frames": len(s["lin"]), "first_frame": off, "z_mean": np.nanmean(z), "z_sd": np.nanstd(z),
                 "r_raw_dff": np.corrcoef(z, np.interp(tz, s["dff_t"], s["dff"]))[0, 1],
                 "r_smoothed_dff": max(match.values()), "at_lag_s": max(match, key=match.get),
                 "held_first": runs[0], "held_last": runs[-1],
                 "lag_of_peak_|r|_s": lags[np.argmax(np.abs(cc))] / 30, "peak_|r|": np.max(np.abs(cc))})
fpdf = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["group", "subject", "start"])
print(fpdf.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("\nRecordings and mice per group (legend of Figure 4B: Anxa1 9 mice 9 recordings, DAT 5 and 7, dLight-dCP 6 and 8, dLight-cCP 6 and 7):")
print(fpdf.groupby("group").agg(recordings=("subject", "size"), mice=("subject", "nunique")).to_string())
near = fpdf["lag_of_peak_|r|_s"].abs() <= 0.5
print(f"Recordings whose speed-signal correlation peaks within 0.5 s of zero lag: {near.sum()} of {len(fpdf)} "
      f"(median peak |r| {fpdf[near]['peak_|r|'].median():.3f}); the others: median peak |r| {fpdf[~near]['peak_|r|'].median():.3f}")

Recordings whose speed-signal correlation peaks within 0.5 s of zero lag: 16 of 31 (median peak |r| 0.138); the others: median peak |r| 0.112

The FiberPhotometrySeriesZScored series of each open field recording (mean 0, s.d. 1) is not the dF/F at the same times z-scored: it correlates with the raw dF/F at 0.42 to 0.92, and better with a 0.2 s running mean of it, best at the lag given (at_lag_s, the z sample matching the dF/F that much earlier). Its first 7 or 8 samples, and in most files its last 8, are held constant, the mark of a centred smoothing window of about half a second. The series is described as session-level z-scored and aligned to the behaviour frames, but its smoothing and the 0.1 s lag are not documented. It is used as the dandiset's processed trace, put on the frames by its starting_time (first_frame). Seven recordings hold under 13 minutes of photometry, against the 20 minute sessions of the Methods. The lag at which speed and signal correlate most is within 0.5 s of zero in 16 of 31 recordings; the correlations are weak at every lag (median peak |r| 0.14 and 0.11), so this check is weak. The photometry and the behaviour frames are consistent with one clock where it can be checked, not shown to share it in every recording. The recording counts differ from the legend's by one or two in three groups (Anxa1 10 against 9, DAT 6 against 7, dLight-dCP 5 mice against 6), and the dandiset does not say which recordings the paper used; all are used here.

SHIFTS = list(range(-45, 46, 3))
krows = []
for s in oft:
    st, d = s["pose_step6"], s["dist"]
    cl = {}
    for l in range(0, 31):          # kinematics frame i against pose frame i + l
        a = st[l:l + len(d)]; ok = np.isfinite(a) & np.isfinite(d)
        cl[l] = np.corrcoef(a[ok], d[ok])[0, 1]
    fit = anxa1.label_speed_fit(s["lin"], s["motif"], SHIFTS)
    krows.append({"subject": s["subject"], "group": s["group"], "path": s["path"], "fp": s["fp"], "kin_t0": s["kin_t0"], "motif_t0": s["motif_t0"], "pose minus kinematics frames": s["n_pose"] - len(s["lin"]),
                  "motif minus kinematics frames": len(s["motif"]) - len(s["lin"]),
                  "kinematics lag (pose frames)": max(cl, key=cl.get), "best motif shift": max(fit, key=fit.get),

In every open field file the kinematics and the motif labels start at t = 0, as the pose does, and both have 30 frames fewer than the pose. The kinematics match the pose with no lag (the pose step correlates best with distance_moved at lag 0 in the count shown), so they are on the pose frames and the 30 missing frames are at the end. The motif labels are not: speed is explained best by the labels moved later by the median shift printed, about half the 30-frame VAME window, so a stored label describes the window that starts at its frame. The files say nothing of this; motif onsets as stored come early by that much. This bears on the motif-onset AUCs (shown below with the labels moved), not on the speed correlations of fig4b, which use the kinematics and the photometry, whose starting_time matches its own dF/F timestamps. Of the 19 files whose kinematics are not at lag 0 to the pose, five hold photometry (listed); fig4b is also run with their speed moved by that lag.

orows = []

    z = anxa1.zscore(s["dff"])
    g, P, kept = anxa1.peri(s["t"], z, s["on"], -1, 1)
    gs, Ps, _ = anxa1.peri(s["t"], z, s["on"] + 2.0, -1, 1)
    resp = lambda Q, gg: (Q[:, (gg >= 0) & (gg <= 1)].mean(1) - Q[:, (gg >= -1) & (gg < 0)].mean(1)).mean()
    orows.append({"subject": s["subject"], "genotype": s["genotype"], "location": s["location"], "indicator": s["indicator"],
                  "power_mW": float(np.unique(s["power"])[0]), "n_powers": len(np.unique(s["power"])),

The evoked release sessions are four Anxa1-Flp mice with dLight1.3b, two with the fiber in dCP and two in cCP, each at five powers in separate sessions of about 20 minutes, with 1 s trains of 40 pulses at 40 Hz every 4 s (some trains are cut short, with 1 to 39 pulses). The dF/F rises after train onsets and not 2 s later, so the stimulation table and the photometry share a clock. The session descriptions call these self-stimulation sessions in which the mouse nosepoked, but the trains come at fixed 4 s intervals. All four mice are listed as WT in their open field files and as Anxa1-flp here (checked below).

Event times equal the annotated video frame divided by 60, the video rate. Distances in cm are the pixel distance divided by the session's reference length in pixels, a 1 cm reference, so they are in cm as stated. In the photometry sessions most events (746 of 1089) are made with the mouth, and 673 carry no distance; these are the water drop sessions of Figure 3, stored as reaching sessions. Some sessions of the 6-OHDA tail striatum cohort hold hundreds of unknown events; that cohort is not in the preprint.

    fake = rng_check.uniform(s["t"][0] + 3, s["t"][-1] - 3, 200)
    gf, Pf, _ = anxa1.peri(s["t"], z, fake, -2, 2)

The mean signal around the annotated drop retrievals varies more than around 200 random times in every recording, so events and photometry are consistent with one clock. Part of the contrast is the noise of a mean over few events, so it cannot tell in sessions with 1 to 3 events. The dandiset holds more recordings than the legend counts in every group, and does not say which were used. The session descriptions say the GCaMP recordings are of SN cell bodies, while the fiber table and the indicator descriptions place them in dCP, as the paper does; the fiber table is followed here. The group of each recording is taken from its indicator, line and fiber site.

The arrow maze sessions last 10 minutes at 30 fps, as in the Methods, and each mouse has four days. The TeTx cohort has 17 controls against the legend's 18. The files hold pose only: no end-zone entries, rewards or arena geometry, so the transitions and rewards of Figure 6D cannot be counted. About 0.2% of tail base steps are jumps of more than 30 pixels (1.5 cm in 33 ms), which a mean speed is sensitive to.

No file holds a nosepoke, reward, end-zone or trial table: the evoked release files hold the photometry and the stimulation epochs, the arrow maze files hold pose and the external video only, and the reaching files hold the annotated events, photometry or a pose model. The self-stimulation, ratio-task and maze-learning data of Figures 3I to 3O and 6D are therefore not in the dandiset.

GEO GSE282753, the paper's only RNA-seq deposit, holds one count table: MitoPark and control DANs at 10 weeks, 5 MitoPark mice (the legend's MP-early n = 5) and 7 controls, each mouse with 3 to 12 technical libraries. The supplementary files are this count table and an RPKM table of the same MitoPark libraries, and the series' design and its 92 samples describe MitoPark and control mice only, so there is no cMfn2KO table. The counts are integers, as DESeq2 and edgeR need.

fig1b-anxa1-downregulated-rnaseq (MitoPark half)¶

In bulk RNA-seq of sorted midbrain DANs, both early-stage mitochondrial PD models (cMfn2KO-early and MP-early) show significant downregulation of the Anxa1 transcript among DAN subtype markers.

Criterion: Anxa1 downregulated against its controls at FDR < 0.05 in both models. GEO holds no differential expression results of the paper, so the readings are DESeq2 and edgeR with default settings on the deposited counts, judged only where both agree. The deposit lacks the cMfn2KO-early data, so that half cannot be tested and the claim stays blocked; the MitoPark half is run and reported, as the answered question asks. The mouse is the unit: technical libraries are summed per mouse (reading a); each library as a sample is a variant. All 5 MitoPark and 7 control mice are used. DESeq2 is pydeseq2; edgeR is its Python port edgepy (TMM, common and tagwise dispersions, exact test), since R is not in the entry's environment.

for unit, M in [("a mouse (libraries summed)", by_mouse), ("variant: library", GEO)]:

    de, ed = anxa1.deseq2(M, g), anxa1.edger_exact(M, g)

Result: blocked (other). The MitoPark half holds. With libraries summed per mouse (5 MitoPark, 7 controls), Anxa1 is down in MitoPark by DESeq2 (log2 fold change -1.02, FDR 2.9e-05) and by edgeR (-0.99, FDR 7.5e-04), and both agree with each library as a sample (-0.93, FDR 5.0e-08 and 6.2e-08). Anxa1 counts per million are 90 to 222 in the MitoPark mice and 258 to 446 in the controls. GSE282753 holds no cMfn2KO counts (its supplementary files are the MitoPark counts and RPKM only, and its 92 samples are MitoPark and control libraries), so the other half of the claim cannot be tested, and the claim stays blocked.

figs2-evoked-da-dcp-ccp¶

Optogenetic activation of Anxa1+ DANs evokes DA release in the dCP at varying intensities, and the evoked release in the cCP has a lower amplitude.

Criterion: dLight z-scored signal aligned to the 1 s ChRmine trains; peak of the mean evoked response within 0 to 1 s and within 0 to 2 s of onset; reproduced when the dCP peak exceeds the pre-stimulus baseline and the cCP peak is lower than the dCP peak, per recording, by a two-sided unpaired t-test at p < 0.05. After the answered question the criterion names the readings: (a) each session's mean over all trains, all powers pooled, the session as unit (10 dCP against 10 cCP sessions); (b) each power alone, the session as unit (2 against 2 at each of five powers). The baseline is the mean over (i) 1 s and (ii) 2 s before train onset. The dandiset holds dF/F, not z-scores, so the header's two z-scorings are run: over the session, and against the baseline window before each train (the same 1 s or 2 s). A per-mouse summary is reported, not judged (two mice per site). dCP and cCP are different mice, so no paired test applies.

In [15]:
def evoked(s, zr, bl):
    x = anxa1.zscore(s["dff"]) if zr == "session" else s["dff"]
    g, P, kept = anxa1.peri(s["t"], x, s["on"], -2.0, 3.0)
    if zr == "baseline":
        pre = P[:, (g >= -bl) & (g < 0)]
        P = (P - pre.mean(1, keepdims=True)) / pre.std(1, keepdims=True)
    return g, P.mean(0), len(kept)

erows, traces = [], {}
for s in opto:
    for zr in ("session", "baseline"):
        for bl in (1.0, 2.0):
            g, m, n = evoked(s, zr, bl)
            traces[(s["subject"], float(s["power"][0]), zr, bl)] = (g, m)
            pre = m[(g >= -bl) & (g < 0)]
            for w in (1.0, 2.0):
                erows.append({"site": "dCP" if s["location"].startswith("Dorsal") else "cCP", "subject": s["subject"],
                              "power_mW": float(s["power"][0]), "zscore": zr, "baseline_s": bl, "window_s": w, "trains": n,
                              "trains_all": len(s["on"]), "peak": m[(g >= 0) & (g <= w)].max(), "baseline": pre.mean(), "pre_max": pre.max()})
ev = pd.DataFrame(erows)
ev["peak_minus_baseline"] = ev.peak - ev.baseline
per_sess = ev.drop_duplicates(["subject", "power_mW"])
print(f"Trains per session kept (window -2 to 3 s inside the recording): {per_sess.trains.min()} to {per_sess.trains.max()}; "
      f"dropped {int((per_sess.trains_all - per_sess.trains).sum())} of {int(per_sess.trains_all.sum())}")

def site_test(g):
    d, c = g[g.site == "dCP"], g[g.site == "cCP"]
    t = stats.ttest_ind(d.peak, c.peak)
    return {"n dCP": len(d), "n cCP": len(c), "dCP peak": d.peak.mean(), "cCP peak": c.peak.mean(),
            "dCP peak > baseline": f"{(d.peak > d.baseline).sum()}/{len(d)}",
            "dCP peak > pre-train max": f"{(d.peak > d.pre_max).sum()}/{len(d)}",
            "t": t.statistic, "p": t.pvalue, "cohen d": (d.peak.mean() - c.peak.mean()) / np.sqrt((d.peak.var() + c.peak.var()) / 2),
            "p (peak minus baseline)": stats.ttest_ind(d.peak_minus_baseline, c.peak_minus_baseline).pvalue,
            "holds": bool((d.peak > d.baseline).all() and d.peak.mean() > c.peak.mean() and t.pvalue < 0.05)}

KEYS = ["zscore", "baseline_s", "window_s"]
RA = pd.DataFrame([{**dict(zip(KEYS, k)), **site_test(g)} for k, g in ev.groupby(KEYS)])
print("Reading (a), all powers pooled per session, 10 sessions against 10:")
print(RA.round(4).to_string(index=False))
RB = pd.DataFrame([{**dict(zip(KEYS + ["power_mW"], k)), **site_test(g)} for k, g in ev.groupby(KEYS + ["power_mW"])])
print("\nReading (b), each power alone, 2 sessions against 2 (with n = 2 Cohen's d equals t):")
print(RB.drop(columns=["n dCP", "n cCP", "dCP peak > pre-train max"]).round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("\nReading (b), powers at which it holds, of 5:")
print(RB.groupby(KEYS).agg(powers_holding=("holds", "sum"), not_holding=("power_mW", lambda x: list(x[~RB.loc[x.index, "holds"]])),
                           p_min=("p", "min"), p_max=("p", "max"), d_min=("cohen d", "min"), d_max=("cohen d", "max")).round(4).to_string())

Result: reproduced. Under reading (a), all powers pooled per session, the criterion holds with both z-scorings, both baselines and both windows: the dCP peak exceeds the baseline in 10 of 10 sessions and the cCP peak is lower (session z-score 1.21 against 0.61, t = 3.94, p = 0.0010, Cohen's d 1.76; baseline z-score 2.30 against 1.19, p = 0.0041, with the 1 s baseline and 1.93 against 1.03, p = 0.0043, with 2 s). The 0 to 2 s window gives the same peaks as 0 to 1 s. Under reading (b), each power alone with 2 sessions against 2, it holds at 3 or 4 of the 5 powers (p = 0.0039 to 0.037 where it holds); it fails at 2 mW under every combination (p = 0.16 to 0.31) and at 0.1 mW except with the baseline z-score over 1 s (p = 0.056 and 0.11 where it fails). The dCP peak is above the cCP peak in both mice of each site at every power, and peaks rise with power (Spearman rho 0.81 in dCP, 0.985 in cCP). Per mouse, reported and not judged, the mean peak over powers is 1.23 and 1.20 in dCP and 0.56 and 0.66 in cCP. The first reading the criterion lists holds in full, so the outcome is reproduced; reading (b) holds at most powers but not at all. With trains every 4 s, the 2 s baseline starts 2 s after the previous onset, but the mean trace is flat there (-0.175 from -2 to -1 s and -0.174 from -1 to 0 s in dCP, -0.111 and -0.106 in cCP), so the previous response has decayed and the 2 s baseline is not raised by it.

fig3d-anxa1-ramp-to-touch¶

Anxa1+ and DAT+ axons in dCP ramp up before a water drop, peak at contact with it, and return quickly to baseline during water consumption.

Criterion: z-scored signals aligned to the water drop touch; per recording the mean over touches of the AUC in three windows, (a) 1 s windows -2 to -1, -1 to 0 and 0 to 1 s, (b) 2 s windows -4 to -2, -2 to 0 and 0 to 2 s; RM one-way ANOVA with the Geisser-Greenhouse correction and Sidak's post hoc (paired comparisons, Sidak over the three pairs), the recording as unit. Reproduced when, under a reading, the Anxa1 ANOVA has p < 0.05 with window 2 above window 3 at Sidak p < 0.05, and the DAT ANOVA has p < 0.05 with window 2 above window 1. The z-scoring readings of the header are run, (a) over the session and (b) against a pre-event baseline, taken as the first window, which the legend calls the baseline. After the answered questions the criterion names the touch: (i) correct (drop retrieved) only, (ii) every contact with a drop (correct, drop, semidrop); the other labels (empty, a reach to an empty spout, and miss) are used in neither. Every recording of the group and site with at least one event is used, the n used is shown against the legend's, and a per-mouse summary is reported, not judged.

In [17]:
WINDOWS = {"1 s": [(-2, -1), (-1, 0), (0, 1)], "2 s": [(-4, -2), (-2, 0), (0, 2)]}
EVENTS = {"i correct": ["correct"], "ii contact": ["correct", "drop", "semidrop"]}

def drop_aucs(s, labels, windows, zr):
    e = s["events"][s["events"].label.isin(labels)].time.values
    x = anxa1.zscore(s["dff"]) if zr == "session" else s["dff"]
    g, P, kept = anxa1.peri(s["t"], x, e, windows[0][0], windows[2][1])
    if len(kept) == 0:
        return None, 0, len(e)
    if zr == "baseline":
        b = P[:, (g >= windows[0][0]) & (g <= windows[0][1])]
        P = (P - b.mean(1, keepdims=True)) / b.std(1, keepdims=True)
    return [float(anxa1.auc(g, P, *w).mean()) for w in windows], len(kept), len(e)

wrows = []
for s in [s for s in reach if s["fp"]]:
    for en, labels in EVENTS.items():
        for wn, ws in WINDOWS.items():
            for zr in ("session", "baseline"):
                a, n, n_all = drop_aucs(s, labels, ws, zr)
                wrows.append({"group": s["fp_group"], "subject": s["subject"], "start": s["start"][:16], "events": en,
                              "windows": wn, "zscore": zr, "n_events": n_all, "kept": n,
                              **({f"auc{i + 1}": a[i] for i in range(3)} if a else {})})
W = pd.DataFrame(wrows)
dropped = W[W.auc1.isna()].drop_duplicates(["subject", "start", "events"])
print("Recordings without any usable event, by event set:", dropped.groupby("events").size().to_dict())
lost = W[W.zscore == "session"].assign(lost=lambda d: d.n_events - d.kept.fillna(0)).groupby(["events", "windows"]).agg(events=("n_events", "sum"), lost=("lost", "sum"))
print("Events, and events whose window left the recording:"); print(lost.to_string())
W = W.dropna(subset=["auc1"])

def window_tests(g):
    v = g[["auc1", "auc2", "auc3"]].values
    r = anxa1.rm_oneway(v)
    ph = anxa1.paired_sidak(v, [(0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 2)])
    return {"n": len(v), "mice": g.subject.nunique(), "mean auc1": v[:, 0].mean(), "mean auc2": v[:, 1].mean(), "mean auc3": v[:, 2].mean(),
            "F": r["F"], "df": f"{r['df1']:.2f}, {r['df2']:.2f}", "p": r["p"],
            "Sidak 1v2": ph["p Sidak"][0], "Sidak 1v3": ph["p Sidak"][1], "Sidak 2v3": ph["p Sidak"][2]}

TESTS = pd.DataFrame([{"group": k[0], "events": k[1], "windows": k[2], "zscore": k[3], **window_tests(g)}
                      for k, g in W.groupby(["group", "events", "windows", "zscore"])])
def show(group):
    print(TESTS[TESTS.group == group].drop(columns="group").round(4).to_string(index=False))
for grp in ["Anxa1 GCaMP-dCP", "DAT GCaMP-dCP"]:
    print("\n" + grp); show(grp)

def mean_traces(group, labels, lo=-5, hi=5):
    out = []
    for s in [s for s in reach if s["fp"] and s["fp_group"] == group]:
        e = s["events"][s["events"].label.isin(labels)].time.values
        g, P, kept = anxa1.peri(s["t"], anxa1.zscore(s["dff"]), e, lo, hi)
        if len(kept):
            out.append(P.mean(0))
    return g, np.array(out)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(15, 3.2), sharey=True)
rng_all = []
for ax, grp in zip(axes, anxa1.FP_GROUPS):
    g, M = mean_traces(grp, ["correct"])
    m, se = M.mean(0), M.std(0) / np.sqrt(len(M))
    rng_all += [m.min(), m.max()]
    ax.plot(g, m, color="k"); ax.fill_between(g, m - se, m + se, color="0.8")
    for x in (-2, -1, 0, 1): ax.axvline(x, color="0.85", lw=0.5)
    ax.set_title(f"{grp} (n={len(M)})"); ax.set_xlabel("time from drop retrieval (s)")
    print(f"{grp}: mean trace peaks at {g[np.argmax(m)]:+.2f} s, value {m.max():.2f}; at 0 s {m[np.argmin(np.abs(g))]:.2f}")
axes[0].set_ylabel("z (session)"); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
print(f"plotted means range {min(rng_all):.2f} to {max(rng_all):.2f}")

Result: not reproduced. Under no reading do both parts hold. The DAT part fails in all eight combinations of events, windows and z-scoring (ANOVA p = 0.050 to 0.145, window 1 against 2 Sidak p = 0.35 to 0.9985). The Anxa1 part holds only with every contact as the touch, 1 s windows and the session z-score (ANOVA p = 0.048, window 2 above window 3 at Sidak p = 0.045); with the drop retrievals alone its ANOVA has p = 0.0139 to 0.109 and window 2 against 3 Sidak p = 0.107 to 0.211. The mean Anxa1 trace does peak at +0.03 s from the drop retrieval (z 0.25), the DAT trace at +2.88 s. The answered questions fixed the event readings and the recordings as they were already run, so the numbers and the outcome are unchanged. Every recording has at least one event under both event readings: 15 Anxa1 recordings of 6 mice and 8 DAT of 5, against the legend's 10 of 7 and 4 of 3; 3 to 5 of 661 and 731 events are lost where the window leaves the recording. Per mouse, reported and not judged, the DAT ANOVA has p = 0.10 to 0.25, the Anxa1 ANOVA p = 0.027 to 0.15 and its window 2 against 3 Sidak p = 0.032 to 0.16. Mouse 687662 is anxa1-flp in its open field file and Dat_cre here; without it the DAT part still fails in every reading (ANOVA p = 0.055 to 0.143, window 1 against 2 Sidak p = 0.46 to 0.99).

fig3e-dlight-dcp-ccp-reward¶

DA release in dCP follows the same ramp-and-drop dynamics as Anxa1+ axons, while in cCP it shows a classical reward-related profile, ramping before contact and peaking during consumption before returning to baseline.

Criterion: as fig3d, with the same window, event and recording readings (the event and recording readings fixed by the answered questions). Reproduced when, under a reading, dLight-dCP has ANOVA p < 0.05 with window 2 above window 3 at Sidak p < 0.05, and dLight-cCP has ANOVA p < 0.05 with windows 2 and 3 both above window 1 at Sidak p < 0.05. The test tables are those computed above.

Result: not reproduced. The dCP part, the point of the claim (DA in dCP follows the Anxa1 ramp and drop), does not hold under any reading: its ANOVA has p = 0.21 to 0.76 and window 2 against 3 Sidak p = 0.30 to 0.90. The cCP profile is there: its ANOVA has p = 0.0001 to 0.0014 under every reading, window 3 is above window 1 at Sidak p = 0.0005 to 0.0012, and window 2 is above window 1 at Sidak p < 0.05 in 5 of 8 combinations (for example drop retrievals, 1 s windows, session z: F = 13.42, p = 0.0006; 1 against 2 Sidak p = 0.041; 1 against 3 p = 0.0006), so the cCP part holds in 5 of 8. The criterion needs both parts under one reading, which never happens. This was partially reproduced before the first verification; the verifier judged it not reproduced, since the dCP part fails everywhere, and the outcome follows that. The dandiset gives 21 dCP recordings of 7 mice and 15 cCP of 6, against the legend's 13 of 6 and 11 of 6. Per mouse, reported and not judged, the dCP ANOVA has p = 0.46 to 0.87 and the cCP ANOVA p = 0.0006 to 0.018.

fig3fg-auc-change-from-baseline¶

Against the baseline window, the legend lists three AUC changes, the second window of DAT GCaMP-dCP (p = 0.0308) and of dLight-cCP (p = 0.0028) and the third window of dLight-cCP (p = 0.0148), with only the dLight-cCP second window marked significant; the other groups and windows are not listed.

Criterion: per recording the AUC of windows 2 and 3 minus window 1; one-sample two-tailed t-test against 0, Bonferroni over eight tests (four groups, two windows) or over four (per window). Reproduced when, under a window reading, the dLight-cCP second-window change is positive and significant after Bonferroni under a family, and the other two listed changes are positive. The claims file names both z-scorings and ranks neither, so both are judged. Under the baseline z-score the first window is the baseline the trace is z-scored against.

for (en, wn, zr), g0 in W.groupby(["events", "windows", "zscore"]):
    for grp in anxa1.FP_GROUPS:
        g = g0[g0.group == grp]

            dlt = g[f"auc{w}"] - g.auc1
            t = stats.ttest_1samp(dlt, 0)
            crow.append({"events": en, "windows": wn, "zscore": zr, "group": grp, "window": w, "n": len(dlt),
                         "mean change": dlt.mean(), "p raw": t.pvalue})
C = pd.DataFrame(crow)

Result: partially reproduced. The claims file names two z-scorings and judges the claim under both; it holds under one and fails under the other. With the baseline z-score the dLight-cCP second-window change is positive and significant after Bonferroni over four tests in all four event and window combinations (p = 0.020 to 0.049) and over eight with 2 s windows (p = 0.040 and 0.047), with the DAT second (0.13 to 0.28) and cCP third (1.43 to 1.77) changes positive. With the session z-score the cCP second-window change (0.29 to 0.36) is not significant after either correction (four tests p = 0.055 to 0.31). In every reading the dLight-cCP third window departs from the first far more than the second does (raw p = 0.0002 to 0.0004 against 0.005 to 0.077), the reverse of the legend, where the second (p = 0.0028) is stronger than the third (p = 0.0148) and only the second is marked. The DAT second-window change is positive but far from significant (raw p = 0.13 to 0.89). This was blocked as methods underspecified before the first verification, on the view that the z-scoring decides; the verifier judged it partially reproduced, as it holds under one of the claims file's readings only, and the outcome follows that.

fig4b-speed-correlation-dcp¶

Anxa1+ axonal activity in the dCP correlates positively with linear speed during open field exploration, above a shuffled control, and DA release in dCP shows a similar correlation.

Criterion: per recording, Pearson's r over the session between the z-scored photometry and linear speed, against the same with the signal shuffled, (a) a random permutation of samples and (b) a circular shift by a random lag; two-sided paired t-test over recordings; reproduced when, under a reading, both Anxa1 GCaMP-dCP and dLight-dCP have a mean r above 0 and above the shuffle at p < 0.05. The dandiset's 30 Hz z-scored trace (the paper's time base) and its linear_velocity are used. The shuffled value of a recording is the mean over 100 shuffles (a standard choice that cannot change the outcome, as shuffled r is near 0). The Wilcoxon signed-rank test is a variant.

rng_4b = np.random.default_rng(4)
crows = []
for s in fp:
    z, v, _ = anxa1.frame_aligned(s)
    ok = np.isfinite(z) & np.isfinite(v)
    z, v = z[ok], v[ok]
    n = len(z)
    crows.append({"group": s["group"], "subject": s["subject"], "start": s["start"][:16], "samples": n,
                  "r": np.corrcoef(z, v)[0, 1],
                  "r permuted": np.mean([np.corrcoef(rng_4b.permutation(z), v)[0, 1] for _ in range(100)]),
                  "r circular": np.mean([np.corrcoef(np.roll(z, rng_4b.integers(1, n)), v)[0, 1] for _ in range(100)])})
CR = pd.DataFrame(crows).sort_values(["group", "subject", "start"])
print(CR.round(4).to_string(index=False))
def corr_tests(g):
    out = {"recordings": len(g), "mice": g.subject.nunique(), "mean r": g.r.mean(), "r > 0": f"{(g.r > 0).sum()}/{len(g)}"}
    for sh in ("permuted", "circular"):
        out[f"t-test p vs {sh}"] = stats.ttest_rel(g.r, g[f"r {sh}"]).pvalue
        out[f"Wilcoxon p vs {sh}"] = stats.wilcoxon(g.r, g[f"r {sh}"]).pvalue
    out["mean r per mouse"] = g.groupby("subject").r.mean().round(3).to_dict()
    return out

Result: not reproduced. dLight-dCP correlates with speed above both shuffles (mean r = 0.067, 7 of 8 recordings positive, paired t-test p = 0.010 against permutation and 0.008 against circular shifts; Wilcoxon p = 0.023 and 0.016). Anxa1 GCaMP-dCP is positive in 9 of 10 recordings but not significantly (mean r = 0.066, p = 0.080 and 0.071, Wilcoxon p = 0.064); one recording (842430) is at r = -0.17. Without the seven short recordings, Anxa1 p = 0.097 and 0.089, and dLight-dCP p = 0.059 against permutation and 0.0499 against circular shifts. DAT GCaMP-dCP, with no test in the legend, has mean r = 0.032 (p = 0.22). Without mouse 687662, whose water drop file says Dat_cre, Anxa1 has mean r = 0.057, 7 of 8 positive, p = 0.21 and 0.18.

Of the 19 open field files whose kinematics are not at lag 0 to the pose, five hold photometry (Anxa1 687642 at 5 frames and 816510 at 1, dLight-dCP 776769 at 1 and 829248 at 30, dLight-cCP 842388 at 1). With their speed moved by that lag, Anxa1 p = 0.082 and 0.073 and dLight-dCP p = 0.028 and 0.023 (6 of 8 positive, Wilcoxon p = 0.0547 against permutation), so the result does not change. The speed-signal correlation of the Anxa1 recordings peaks within 0.5 s of zero lag in 5 of 10; the other five peak at -2.3 to 2.1 s, on both sides of zero, with peak |r| 0.09 to 0.19. That the photometry and the speed share one clock is checked where the files allow it, not shown for every recording, so an offset in some recordings is not ruled out.

The criterion needs both groups at p < 0.05 under one reading, and Anxa1, the subject of the claim, misses it in every reading (p = 0.064 to 0.21). As for fig3e, whose main part fails in every reading, this is a failure of the claim and not a partial result. This was partially reproduced before the first verification; the verifier judged it not reproduced in rounds 1 and 2, the change was proposed after round 2, and the third round agreed with it, so the outcome follows that.

fig4c-vame-motifs¶

Unsupervised VAME analysis of open field pose identifies 37 kinematic motifs, grouped into action categories.

Criterion: the count of distinct motif labels in the paper's motif labelling; tolerance 0. The dandiset holds one labelling, VAME_42/MotifSeries, in every open field file; whether it is the paper's 37-motif labelling is checked against the motif numbers the Results name. The claims file's header says the motif claims use the paper's label per frame if the dataset holds it, and that a new VAME fit is not a basis for an outcome.

Result: blocked (data missing). The dandiset's VAME labelling has 42 distinct labels (0 to 41), 39 of them above 1% of frames, where the paper reports 37 motifs (47 above the 1% threshold, 10 then merged, by the Methods). It is not the paper's labelling: motif 42, which the Results name, is not a label of the dandiset, and motif 28, named as a stationary motif increased in MP-middle mice, is never used by the 108 mice of Figure 5. No motif category is stored. The paper's labelling is therefore not in the dandiset, and by the claims file's header this claim and those resting on it (fig4e, fig4f, fig4h, fig5g, fig5h, fig5i, fig5j and fig5m) have no basis for an outcome. Before the first verification this claim was judged not reproduced (42 labels against 37) and fig4e, fig4f, fig4h, fig5g and fig5i were judged on the dandiset's labels; the verifier pointed out that this contradicts the header and the blocking of fig5j and fig5m on the same evidence. The analyses below are kept, on the dandiset's labels, and decide nothing.

fig4f-auc-correlations¶

Across motifs, the onset AUC of Anxa1+ terminal activity correlates positively with that of dLight in dCP (R = 0.70) and negatively with that of dLight in cCP (R = -0.52).

Criterion: per motif, the AUC from 0 to 1 s after onset (first frame of a run of the label) of the z-scored signal, then Pearson's R over motifs between groups. Readings: (a) all onsets of a group pooled, then the mean trace, or (b) the mean per recording, then the mean over recordings; (i) the AUC as is, or (ii) minus the mean over -1 to 0 s. Reproduced when, under a reading, both R are within tolerance (0.70 +/- 0.07, -0.52 +/- 0.052) and p < 0.01. The dandiset's labels are used (see fig4c), as stored; a motif enters when every group has an onset of it with 1 s of signal on both sides.

Blocked (data missing), as it rests on the paper's motif labelling (fig4c). The test below runs on the dandiset's own labels and is shown, not judged.

In [26]:
NM = 60
grid = np.arange(-30, 31) / 30.0

def onset_aucs(shift=0):
    """Mean onset traces and 0 to 1 s AUCs per motif and group, the labels shifted by `shift` frames."""
    onset_traces = {grp: {k: [] for k in range(NM)} for grp in anxa1.FP_GROUPS}
    per_rec = {grp: [] for grp in anxa1.FP_GROUPS}
    n_on = {grp: np.zeros(NM, int) for grp in anxa1.FP_GROUPS}
    for s in fp:
        z, v, m = anxa1.frame_aligned(s, shift)
        rec = np.full((NM, len(grid)), np.nan)
        for k, idx in anxa1.motif_onsets(m).items():
            idx = idx[(idx >= 30) & (idx + 30 < len(z))]
            if len(idx) == 0: continue
            tr = np.stack([z[i - 30:i + 31] for i in idx])
            tr = tr[np.isfinite(tr).all(1)]
            if len(tr) == 0: continue
            rec[k] = tr.mean(0); onset_traces[s["group"]][k].append(tr); n_on[s["group"]][k] += len(tr)
        per_rec[s["group"]].append(rec)
    out = {}
    for grp in anxa1.FP_GROUPS:
        for base in (False, True):
            out[(grp, "a pooled", base)] = np.array([motif_auc(np.concatenate(onset_traces[grp][k]).mean(0), base)
                                                     if onset_traces[grp][k] else np.nan for k in range(NM)])
            out[(grp, "b per recording", base)] = np.nanmean(np.stack([motif_auc(r, base) for r in per_rec[grp]]), 0)
    return out, n_on

def motif_auc(trace, base):
    a = anxa1.auc(grid, trace, 0, 1)
    return a - trace[..., (grid >= -1) & (grid < 0)].mean(-1) * 1.0 if base else a

print("Onsets per motif, Anxa1: median", int(np.median(n_onsets["Anxa1 GCaMP-dCP"][common])), "min", n_onsets["Anxa1 GCaMP-dCP"][common].min())

fig4h-auc-motif-speed¶

The onset AUC of Anxa1+ terminal activity is highly correlated with mean motif linear speed across motifs (R = 0.83).

Criterion: the AUC readings of fig4f; motif speed is the mean linear speed over the frames of the motif, over the Anxa1 recordings or over all mice of the motif set (all open field files), both run. Reproduced when R is within 0.83 +/- 0.083 and p < 0.01 under a reading.

Blocked (data missing), as it rests on the paper's motif labelling (fig4c). The test below runs on the dandiset's own labels and is shown, not judged.

In [27]:
def motif_speed(sessions, shift=0):
    tot, n = np.zeros(NM), np.zeros(NM)
    for s in sessions:
        m = anxa1.shift_labels(s["motif"], shift)
        v = s["lin"][:len(m)]
        ok = np.isfinite(v) & (m >= 0)
        tot += np.bincount(m[ok], weights=v[ok], minlength=NM); n += np.bincount(m[ok], minlength=NM)
    return tot / np.maximum(n, 1)
SPEED = {"Anxa1 recordings": motif_speed([s for s in fp if s["group"] == "Anxa1 GCaMP-dCP"]), "all open field files": motif_speed(oft)}

            rows.append({"averaging": rd, "baseline subtracted": base, "speed over": sp, "R": r[0], "p": r[1],
                         "within tolerance": abs(r[0] - 0.83) <= 0.083 and r[1] < 0.01})

On the dandiset's labels as stored, Anxa1 onset AUC correlates positively with mean motif speed under every reading, but below the paper's value: R = 0.62 to 0.68 with baseline subtraction (p < 0.0001) and 0.47 to 0.55 without (p = 0.0003 to 0.0025), none within 0.83 +/- 0.083. The motif-onset AUCs on these labels therefore say little about the claim.

fig4e-anxa1-high-speed-motifs¶

Anxa1+ axon activity is associated with the onset of high-speed motifs regardless of action type, as is DA in dCP, while DA in cCP rises strongly after the onset of low-speed motifs.

Criterion: judged by fig4f and fig4h, and in addition, for "independently of the action type", a positive Spearman correlation of Anxa1 AUC (0 to 1 s) with motif speed within at least two action categories, and for cCP a negative correlation of its AUC with motif speed. The dandiset holds no category for its motifs, so the within-category part cannot be run. The other parts are below.

The within-category part cannot be run, as the dandiset holds no category for its motifs, and the parts it is judged by (fig4f, fig4h) are blocked.

fig5c-tetx-locomotion¶

Anxa1-TeTx mice show moderate reductions in linear and angular speed in the open field, with a slight increase in immobility time.

Criterion: per mouse, mean linear speed, mean angular speed and immobility time over the session; two-sided unpaired t-test against Ctrl-Tdtomato. Reproduced when both speeds are lower at p < 0.05 and immobility is higher; partially reproduced when one speed is lower at p < 0.05. The dandiset's linear_velocity and angular_velocity are used. It holds no immobility value and the threshold is open, so by the claims file's header immobility is not judged.

In [29]:
O5 = [s for s in oft if s["group"] in anxa1.FIG5_GROUPS]
loco = pd.DataFrame([{"group": s["group"], "subject": s["subject"], "sex": s["sex"], "linear": np.nanmean(s["lin"]),
                      "angular": np.nanmean(s["ang"])} for s in O5])
def ttest_row(ctrl, exp, var):
    a, b = loco[loco.group == ctrl][var], loco[loco.group == exp][var]
    t = stats.ttest_ind(a, b)
    return {"measure": var, "control": ctrl, "group": exp, "n": f"{len(a)}/{len(b)}", "control mean": a.mean(), "group mean": b.mean(),
            "change %": (b.mean() / a.mean() - 1) * 100, "t": t.statistic, "p": t.pvalue,
            "hedges g": (b.mean() - a.mean()) / np.sqrt(((len(a) - 1) * a.var() + (len(b) - 1) * b.var()) / (len(a) + len(b) - 2))}
print(pd.DataFrame([ttest_row("Ctrl-Tdtomato", "Anxa1-TeTx", v) for v in ("linear", "angular")]).round(4).to_string(index=False, formatters={"p": "{:.2e}".format}))
print("\nBy sex (linear, angular means):")
print(loco[loco.group.isin(["Ctrl-Tdtomato", "Anxa1-TeTx"])].groupby(["group", "sex"])[["linear", "angular"]].agg(["mean", "size"]).round(3).to_string())
print("\nMann-Whitney variant:", {v: round(stats.mannwhitneyu(loco[loco.group == "Ctrl-Tdtomato"][v], loco[loco.group == "Anxa1-TeTx"][v]).pvalue, 5) for v in ("linear", "angular")})

fig5e-early-models-locomotion¶

The mild locomotor phenotype and acceleration distribution of Anxa1-silenced mice resemble the early-stage PD models (mild 6-OHDA, MP-early), consistent with a bradykinetic and not an akinetic/rigid profile.

Criterion: for each experimental group, the change of mean linear speed, mean angular speed and immobility against its own control (percent of the control mean), and the acceleration density. Reproduced when the changes of Anxa1-TeTx lie within the range spanned by 6OHDA-low and MP-early, or closer to theirs than to MP-middle's, for at least two of the three measures. Immobility is not in the dandiset (fig5c), so two measures are available.

fig5g-pc1-stage¶

In a PCA of motif usage, PC1 separates the groups by PD stage, with Anxa1-TeTx mice between the early and middle PD models, and PC2 separates middle-stage MitoPark mice from the others.

Criterion: PCA of per-mouse motif usage (fraction of session frames) over all mice of the eight groups, (a) standardized or (b) centred only; the sign of each PC set so that MP-middle has the largest group mean. Reproduced when, under a reading, the Anxa1-TeTx mean on PC1 lies between the early models (6OHDA-low, MP-early) and MP-middle, the controls lie on the low side, and the MP-middle mean on PC2 lies farther from the mean of all other groups than any other group's mean. "Between" is read as above both early-model means and below MP-middle; "controls on the low side" as every control mean below every experimental group's mean. Labels never used by these mice are left out (they have no variance).

Blocked (data missing), as it rests on the paper's motif labelling (fig4c). The test below runs on the dandiset's own labels and is shown, not judged.

In [31]:
U_all = np.stack([np.bincount(s["motif"], minlength=NM) / len(s["motif"]) for s in O5])
grp5 = np.array([s["group"] for s in O5])
mused = np.flatnonzero(U_all.sum(0) > 0)
U5 = U_all[:, mused]
spd5 = motif_speed(O5)[mused]
PCA = {}
rows = []
for sc in ("a standardized", "b centred"):
    X = U5 - U5.mean(0)
    if sc.startswith("a"):
        X = X / U5.std(0, ddof=1)
    u, sv, vt = np.linalg.svd(X, full_matrices=False)
    scores, load = u * sv, vt.copy()
    for pc in range(4):
        if pd.Series(scores[:, pc]).groupby(grp5).mean()["MP-middle"] < 0:
            scores[:, pc] *= -1; load[pc] *= -1
    PCA[sc] = (scores, load, sv ** 2 / np.sum(sv ** 2))
    gm = pd.DataFrame({"PC1": pd.Series(scores[:, 0]).groupby(grp5).mean(), "PC2": pd.Series(scores[:, 1]).groupby(grp5).mean()}).loc[anxa1.FIG5_GROUPS]
    print(f"{sc}: {len(mused)} motifs, {len(O5)} mice, variance explained PC1-4 {np.round(PCA[sc][2][:4], 3).tolist()}")
    print(gm.round(3).T.to_string())
    ctrls, exps = ["Ctrl-Tdtomato", "Ctrl-Asc Acid", "Ctrl-early", "Ctrl-middle"], ["Anxa1-TeTx", "6OHDA-low", "MP-early", "MP-middle"]
    between = gm.PC1["Anxa1-TeTx"] > max(gm.PC1["6OHDA-low"], gm.PC1["MP-early"]) and gm.PC1["Anxa1-TeTx"] < gm.PC1["MP-middle"]
    low = gm.PC1[ctrls].max() < gm.PC1[exps].min()
    dist = {g: abs(gm.PC2[g] - gm.PC2.drop(g).mean()) for g in anxa1.FIG5_GROUPS}
    pc2 = max(dist, key=dist.get) == "MP-middle"
    t_pc1 = stats.ttest_ind(scores[grp5 == "Anxa1-TeTx", 0], scores[grp5 == "Ctrl-Tdtomato", 0])
    rows.append({"scaling": sc, "TeTx between early and middle": between, "controls low": low, "MP-middle farthest on PC2": pc2,
                 "PC2 distances": {k: round(v, 2) for k, v in dist.items()}, "TeTx vs Ctrl-Tdtomato PC1 t-test p": t_pc1.pvalue})
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).drop(columns="PC2 distances").to_string(index=False))
for r in rows: print(r["scaling"], "PC2 distance of each group mean from the mean of the others:", r["PC2 distances"])

        ax.scatter(sco[grp5 == g, 0], sco[grp5 == g, 1], s=10, color=col, label=g)
    ax.set_title(sc); ax.set_xlabel("PC1"); ax.set_ylabel("PC2")
axes[0].legend(fontsize=6); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

fig5i-pc1-motif-speed¶

Motif PC1 values correlate negatively with mean motif speed (R = -0.762), while PC2 shows no significant correlation (R = -0.1494, p = 0.3772), nor do PC3 and PC4.

Criterion: per motif, the PC1 to PC4 loading against mean motif linear speed over all mice (here the mice of the PCA); Pearson R. The magnitude is judged with PC1 oriented as in fig5g. Reproduced when, under a reading of fig5g, |R| for PC1 is within 0.762 +/- 0.0762 with p < 0.0001, and PC2, PC3 and PC4 each have p >= 0.05.

Blocked (data missing), as it rests on the paper's motif labelling (fig4c). The test below runs on the dandiset's own labels and is shown, not judged.

Motif numbers (not deciding)¶

fig5j-tetx-five-motifs, fig5j-shared-and-stage-motifs and fig5m-walk-motif-network rest on the paper's motif numbers, which the dandiset's labels are not (fig4c), so they are blocked, as are all the motif claims. The same tests run on the dandiset's labels show what the labels give; they decide nothing.

fig6c-maze-locomotion¶

In the arrow maze, Anxa1-silenced mice show only a small decrease in linear speed on the fourth day and no change in immobility time.

Criterion: per mouse and day (days 1 and 4), mean linear speed over the 10 min session; RM two-way ANOVA group by day with Sidak's post hoc. Reproduced when the group effect has p < 0.05 with Anxa1-TeTx slower, the Sidak test is p < 0.05 on day 4 only, and immobility shows no group effect or Sidak difference. The dandiset holds pose only, so speed is computed under the header's readings, (a) the tail base and (b) the mean of the six points (snout, four paws, tail base), in pixels per s (one camera, so the scale does not change a test). Smoothing is open; raw positions and positions with DeepLabCut confidence below 0.9 interpolated are both run. Immobility has no value in the dandiset or the paper, so it is not judged. Sidak's test compares the groups by an unpaired t-test on each day, adjusted over the two days (a standard implementation; Prism pools the error term).

Result: not reproduced. Under none of the four speed readings is the day 4 difference significant (Sidak p = 0.11 to 0.41). A group effect with Anxa1-TeTx slower appears only with the tail base and low-confidence positions interpolated (F = 4.98, p = 0.035; -21.8% on day 1 and -17.7% on day 4); with raw tail base positions there is none (p = 0.75), and with the mean of six points TeTx mice are faster (raw, p = 0.021) or not different (p = 0.44). Immobility is not tested. The dandiset has 17 control mice against the legend's 18. The tail base occupies the same pixel extent on every day (medians of the 1st and 99th percentiles 98 to 111 and 567 to 620 px in x, 185 to 232 and 699 to 706 px in y), so the scale does not change between days. The speeds are unsmoothed apart from the interpolation of low-confidence positions, and the mean of six points is noisy (raw speeds 1.5 to 5.9 times those of the tail base in the group means, and a jump on day 4 with low-confidence positions interpolated); the claims file leaves smoothing open, so no other smoothing is applied, and the outcome rests on these noisy measures.

fig6j-reaching-accuracy¶

Control mice improve reaching accuracy over four sessions; Anxa1-TeTx mice have normal accuracy in the first session but fail to improve, and Anxa1-Arch mice show reduced accuracy during the last three sessions with optogenetic inhibition.

Criterion: per mouse and session, the fraction of grasp attempts with the preferred forelimb whose distance from the target is within a threshold, < 0.2 cm (Results) or < 0.1 cm (legend of 6J); RM two-way ANOVA group by day on days 1 and 4 with Sidak's post hoc. Reproduced when, under a reading, the interaction has p < 0.05, controls improve from day 1 to day 4 at Sidak p < 0.05, controls exceed both Anxa1-TeTx and Anxa1-Arch on day 4 at Sidak p < 0.05, and Anxa1-TeTx does not differ from controls on day 1; each single exclusion of a mouse is shown as a variant.

After the answered questions the criterion fixes the rest. Grasp attempts are (a) every labelled reach with a distance, or (b) all but empty and unknown; the preferred forelimb is the paw used most (i) per mouse over all its sessions, or (ii) per session. Day 1 and day 4 are the first and fourth training sessions of each mouse; the files label them test1 and test4, and their dates are checked below. For Arch, a day 1 or day 4 session whose laser label departs from the Methods (off on day 1, on on days 2 to 4) is reported. Controls of both cohorts are one pooled group. The main run uses the mice recorded before the preprint (22 December 2024); all mice with both days are a variant. Sessions of one mouse on one day are pooled. Sidak's tests: controls day 1 against day 4 (paired t-test, Sidak over the three groups), and controls against each silenced group on each day (unpaired t-tests, Sidak over the four comparisons).

PREPRINT = "2024-12-22"

def accuracy(sets, thr, pref="mouse", before=PREPRINT):
    X = RE[RE.label.isin(sets) & RE.phase.isin(["test1", "test4"]) & RE.distance_cm.notna()].copy()
    if before:
        X = X[X.groupby("subject").date.transform("min") < before]
    if pref == "mouse":
        p = RE.groupby("subject").paw.agg(lambda x: x.value_counts().idxmax())
        X = X[X.paw == X.subject.map(p)]
    else:
        p = X.groupby(["subject", "phase"]).paw.agg(lambda x: x.value_counts().idxmax())
        X = X[X.paw.values == p.loc[list(zip(X.subject, X.phase))].values]
    a = X.groupby(["subject", "group", "cohort", "phase"]).agg(acc=("distance_cm", lambda d: (d < thr).mean()), n=("distance_cm", "size")).reset_index()
    both = a.groupby("subject").phase.nunique()
    a = a[a.subject.isin(both[both == 2].index)]
    a["day"] = a.phase.map({"test1": 1, "test4": 4})
    return a

def reach_tests(a):
    an = anxa1.mixed_anova(a, "acc", "day", "group", "subject").set_index("Source")
    g = lambda grp, d: a[(a.group == grp) & (a.day == d)].set_index("subject").acc
    c1, c4 = g("Ctrl", 1), g("Ctrl", 4)
    within = {grp: stats.ttest_rel(g(grp, 1), g(grp, 4).loc[g(grp, 1).index]).pvalue for grp in ["Ctrl", "Anxa1-TeTx", "Anxa1-Arch"]}
    between = {(grp, d): stats.ttest_ind(g("Ctrl", d), g(grp, d)).pvalue for grp in ["Anxa1-TeTx", "Anxa1-Arch"] for d in (1, 4)}
    out = {"mice": a.drop_duplicates("subject").groupby("group").size().to_dict(),
           "interaction F": an.loc["Interaction", "F"], "df": f"{an.loc['Interaction', 'DF1']}, {an.loc['Interaction', 'DF2']}",
           "interaction p": an.loc["Interaction", "p_unc"],
           "ctrl d1": c1.mean(), "ctrl d4": c4.mean(), "tet d1": g("Anxa1-TeTx", 1).mean(), "tet d4": g("Anxa1-TeTx", 4).mean(),
           "arch d1": g("Anxa1-Arch", 1).mean(), "arch d4": g("Anxa1-Arch", 4).mean(),
           "Sidak ctrl d1 vs d4": anxa1.sidak(within["Ctrl"], 3), "Sidak ctrl vs tet d4": anxa1.sidak(between[("Anxa1-TeTx", 4)], 4),
           "Sidak ctrl vs arch d4": anxa1.sidak(between[("Anxa1-Arch", 4)], 4), "Sidak ctrl vs tet d1": anxa1.sidak(between[("Anxa1-TeTx", 1)], 4),
           "Sidak ctrl vs arch d1": anxa1.sidak(between[("Anxa1-Arch", 1)], 4)}
    out["holds"] = (out["interaction p"] < 0.05 and c4.mean() > c1.mean() and out["Sidak ctrl d1 vs d4"] < 0.05
                    and out["ctrl d4"] > out["tet d4"] and out["Sidak ctrl vs tet d4"] < 0.05
                    and out["ctrl d4"] > out["arch d4"] and out["Sidak ctrl vs arch d4"] < 0.05 and out["Sidak ctrl vs tet d1"] >= 0.05)
    return out

Result: partially reproduced. In the main run, the 17 mice recorded before the preprint (8 controls, 4 TeTx and 5 Arch; 8 + 4 + 5 fits the legend's F(2,14)), the control and TeTx parts hold and the Arch part does not. With every labelled reach, the preferred limb per mouse and 0.2 cm, the interaction has F(2, 13) = 4.42, p = 0.034, controls improve from 0.338 to 0.650 (Sidak p = 0.010), controls exceed TeTx on day 4 (0.239, p = 0.0014) and do not differ from them on day 1 (p = 0.994), but Arch on day 4 (0.428) does not differ from controls (p = 0.22); one Arch mouse (842433) has no reach with its preferred limb on one day under this reading and drops out. Without empty and unknown reaches the same parts hold (interaction p = 0.046, control improvement p = 0.020, TeTx below controls p = 0.016) and Arch fails (p = 0.34). With the preferred limb per session all 17 mice enter and the df are the legend's (2, 14), but the interaction misses (p = 0.060, and 0.085 without empty and unknown reaches). The Arch day 4 comparison fails in all eight readings of the main run (Sidak p = 0.044 to 0.34; the one below 0.05, at 0.1 cm, comes with an interaction p of 0.12), and with 0.1 cm the interaction misses in every reading (p = 0.069 to 0.27). Of the single exclusions, none of 16 makes the criterion hold with the limb per mouse and one of 17 with the limb per session (leaving out Arch mouse 828027: interaction p = 0.016, Arch day 4 p = 0.035). The variant with all mice holds at 0.2 cm under all four event and limb readings (interaction p = 0.0030 to 0.028). This departs from the paper's protocol, as the claims file asks to report: in the Arch cohort all 17 mice, controls included, have their day 1 session labelled with the laser switched on after the first reach, where the Methods have it off on day 1; these sessions are used as day 1. Day 4 is labelled laser on, as in the Methods. The outcome is partial and not a failure because each part points the claimed way: on day 4 Arch accuracy is below the controls' in all eight readings of the main run (0.099 to 0.428 against 0.264 to 0.650), but not at Sidak p < 0.05 with an interaction at p < 0.05; the verifier judged it not reproduced, and that disagreement is recorded. The sessions labelled test4 fall 2 to 4 days after test1.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The photometry of the water drop and evoked release sessions is z-scored here under the claims file's two readings, from the dandiset's dF/F; the paper's DoricStudio z-scoring is not known. The open field analyses use the dandiset's own 30 Hz z-scored trace and kinematics. The motif claims are blocked, as the dandiset's VAME labels are not the paper's; their analyses are shown on the dandiset's labels and decide nothing. Every recording of a group is used where the dandiset holds more than the legends count. The arrow maze speed is computed from pose, unsmoothed, since the dandiset has no kinematics for it. The water drop touch and the grasp attempts are read from the annotated event labels in two ways each, the readings the answered questions named. The RNA-seq of the MitoPark half is tested on the GEO counts with pydeseq2 and with edgepy, a Python port of edgeR, with TMM written out in the helper and the GLM dispersion estimators (the port has no estimateDisp), not with the R packages; libraries are summed per mouse. Prism's Sidak tests after the ANOVAs are approximated by t-tests with Sidak adjustment, without Prism's pooled error term.

What was found about the dataset:

  • It holds only behaviour and photometry: no histology, RNA-seq, qPCR or nosepoke counts, so 16 claims of Figures 1 to 3 cannot be tested; no file holds a nosepoke, reward, end-zone or trial table, and the arrow maze has pose only, without the Bonsai end-zone entries, rewards or arena geometry.
  • 86 open field files are named as ses-tmaze sessions (session_id tmaze-...), and groups, cohorts, days and test phases are given only in free text in session_description.
  • Subject genotypes conflict across files (dLight mice are WT in their open field files and Anxa1-flp or Dat_cre elsewhere; 687662 is anxa1-flp and Dat_cre), and mouse 779575 is a control in the open field TeTx experiment and a TeTx mouse in the reaching cohort.
  • The VAME labels (42) are not the paper's 37 numbered motifs and carry no categories. They are stored with starting_time 0, but they explain speed best when placed about 18 frames (0.6 s) later, half the VAME window, so motif onsets as stored come early; this is not documented.
  • The z-scored open field photometry is smoothed and lags the dF/F by about 0.1 s, neither documented; seven recordings hold under 13 minutes of photometry.
  • The dandiset holds more recordings and mice than the legends in the photometry and reaching experiments, and experiments not in the preprint (6-OHDA in tail striatum, anti-Anxa1, a 2025 Arch cohort), without saying which are the paper's.
  • Every Arch-cohort reaching file labels day 1 with the laser switched on after the first reach, where the Methods have the laser off on day 1.
  • GEO GSE282753 holds the MitoPark RNA-seq counts and RPKM (5 MitoPark, 7 control mice) but not the cMfn2KO counts.
  • The evoked release sessions are described as nosepoke self-stimulation, but the trains come every 4 s; the session descriptions call the photometry GCaMP signals SN cell-body recordings while the fiber table places them in dCP.
